**Fieldbook 2.4.1 beta 4** (a beta)
### Fixed - **About** on an Unfiled meeting: its greyed-out button now says to move the meeting to Internal or Partners first, instead of calling it a customer meeting. - **Pasting into notes** from a browser or other app keeps curly quotes, apostrophes, dashes, and accented letters, instead of turning them into symbols such as â€œ and â€™.

**Fieldbook 2.4.1 beta 3** (a beta)
### Added - **Ask about one meeting:** click **Ask** in the toolbar with a meeting open, and a column beside it answers questions about that meeting only, from its transcript, your notes, its AI notes, and its attached files. Cited times open the line beside the conversation. - **Recent questions:** your Ask AI questions and their answers are kept on this Mac for 90 days. Open one again without asking the AI, continue it, or ask it again; matching ones show under **Asked before** as you type in the search field. Turn it off, or clear them, in **Settings › AI**. A meeting moved to the Trash takes its questions with it.
### Changed - **About** works while a meeting is recording or being transcribed, like Move To. Move it to Internal or Partners, then pick the customers it's about; its notes are marked for them once they're written. - **Stakeholders on the Account page** list only people with a name. Speakers not yet named ("Speaker 1", "Speaker 2") still show in their meeting's notes, and join the Account page once you name them in the transcript, with no new AI request. The box says how many unnamed speakers it left out.
### Fixed - **Spreadsheets** (in Files, customer reports, and the licensing library) reach the AI with their dates, percentages, and amounts (2025-11-01, 25%, $1,234.50) instead of raw numbers such as 45962 or 0.25.

**Fieldbook 2.4.1 beta 2** (a beta)
### Added - **Talk time:** a meeting's **Speakers** list shows each person's share of the talk time with a bar, and each side's share under the heading (for example **Internal 52% · Customer 32% · Partner 12% · No side 4%**), so you can see who talked most and least. - **Stakeholders:** in Sales mode, a customer or partner meeting's AI notes have a **Stakeholders** section: each person's stance on your solution (**Champion**, **Supporter**, **Neutral**, or **Detractor**), why, and their own words. Someone talked about but not in the meeting shows who reported it. Each customer's **Account** page lists everyone from its meetings, with their side, their stance now and before, and how often they came up and talked; open a person for their stance in each meeting. **Add Stakeholders…** there reads the last 90 days' meetings from before this, with the quick tasks model. Stances are for you: they stay out of Copy and emails.

Sync with your iPhone and iPad, notes from a device joining the recording of the same meeting, and account summaries working again with Claude.
### Added - **Sync with your iPhone and iPad:** pair an iPhone or iPad once in **File Transfers › Your iPhone and iPad** (**Pair iPhone or iPad…**, scan its code on the device, then **Pair** when the 6 digits match). Whenever Fieldbook is open on both and they're nearby (the same Wi-Fi, a Personal Hotspot, or direct, like AirDrop), your meetings from the last 90 days go to them with their notes, transcripts, and attachments, never audio or voices, and their recordings come to this Mac by themselves to be transcribed. - **Your iPhone and iPad:** each paired device on one line, with when it last synced, how many meetings it has, the recordings that came in today, and **Unpair**. **⋯ › Show Address Code…** helps a paired device that can't find this Mac, such as an iPhone sharing its hotspot. - **Settings › General › Sync with iPhone and iPad** turns it off; nothing is unpaired. - **Notes from your iPhone or iPad join the recording:** notes taken with **Take Notes** on an iPhone or iPad go into the recording of the same calendar meeting, made on this Mac or on another device, under a heading saying where they were typed, with their attachments and the customers the meeting is about. The recording keeps its transcript, nothing is transcribed again, and the separate notes go to the Trash, where you can put them back. Only what comes through a sync joins by itself, and notes with their own to-dos, reminders, or opportunity or issue tags stay separate. - **Your meetings of the next 7 days go to your iPhone and iPad** with each sync (titles, times, and the folder each would be filed in; never invitees or agendas), so a device without your work calendar can still name the meeting it records or takes notes in. - **New in Fieldbook 2.4:** shown once after updating, a short note over the main window with this update's two big things.
### Changed - **Local Network:** macOS's question now says Fieldbook also answers the iPhones and iPads you paired with it, while it's open.
### Fixed - **Account summaries with Claude:** with Anthropic as the AI service, writing or rewriting an account summary failed at once with "The compiled grammar is too large". It works again. - **Deleting a label or customer with archived meetings:** the message that refuses now says its meetings are in **Archive**, since they don't show in its list.

Emails tagged with the opportunity or issue they're about, **Live** in the toolbar, File Transfers on a Personal Hotspot, and Zoom for Government in **Today**.
### Added - **Zoom for Government:** **Join** in **Today** works with Zoom for Government links, the menu bar's next meetings show them as Zoom, and a Zoom for Government call in a browser is treated as a call, like a Zoom call. - **Emails about an opportunity or issue:** **About** in an open email tags it with one of the customer's open opportunities or issues. Tagged emails show what they're about in the list, and each opportunity and issue lists its emails ("3 meetings and 2 emails count toward it"). The account summary treats them as the best evidence for that opportunity or issue, and offers an **Update** when you tag one. - **A line for its notes:** with AI set up, tagging an email drafts a dated line for the opportunity's or issue's notes ("10-15-26 - Email from Dana Ruiz - …"). It waits in the email, under the issue's notes, and above the opportunity's notes; **Add to Notes** adds it, and nothing changes until you do. - **New Issue from This Email…:** starts an issue with the ticket number, title, and opened date from the email, and your AI's line as its notes. The email is tagged with it.
### Changed - **Inbox:** each email is filed in a folder's **Emails**, about **Background**, an opportunity, an issue, or **A new issue** (with its ticket and title from the subject). A subject with a known issue's ticket number suggests that issue. An email no customer matches waits unticked until you pick a folder. **New meeting** is no longer in the Inbox; **More…** and **Add Files** still make a meeting from an email. - **Live transcript:** **Live** is now in the toolbar and turns the live transcript and its pane on or off together, during a call too. Off, live transcribing stops and earlier meetings can transcribe; on again, it picks up from then, with the earlier lines kept. Settings › Transcription no longer has its own switch for it. - **Opportunities:** an opportunity's link is saved as you type or paste it, as an issue's is; there's no Save button. - **File Transfers:** the activity log notes each address a send tries and how far it gets, and the Mac's network and each connection while receiving, to find out why a send doesn't go through (**Help › Save Diagnostic Report…**). Never the key or file names. - **Send to Another Fieldbook:** a typed address or name is used only when it's on the local network, as File Transfers always meant; anything else says it isn't on the local network, and nothing is sent. - **Updates:** Sparkle, which installs Fieldbook's updates, is now version 2.10.1 (bug fixes). - Calendars you tick are remembered without their names or accounts. - **AI:** AI answers may show ‹ › where your meetings, notes, or files had < or >: Fieldbook marks them so text in your material is never taken as an instruction.
### Fixed - **Launch:** Fieldbook no longer waits at launch when macOS's screen recording check doesn't answer; it goes on after 10 seconds. - **Today:** Join opens only real meeting links. On Webex, that's a meeting, Personal Room, or webinar link, never the call-in list, a recording, or another page on the Webex site. - A calendar you unticked in **Settings › Meetings › Calendars** no longer comes back ticked after it syncs again. - **Inbox:** **Undo** after filing emails to **Emails** now takes them back. - **Issues and Opportunities:** typing in an issue or an opportunity's notes no longer makes Fieldbook pause every few seconds on a large library or one in Google Drive. Update All now checks only the customer you changed, and not at all for a link, amount, or date, which the AI never reads. - **Inbox:** picking a folder or what an email is about no longer widens the Inbox past its edges when a customer's name or an opportunity's or issue's title is long; the menus keep their widths and cut long names short. An open email's **About** button does the same. - **File Transfers on a Personal Hotspot:** on a hotspot that gives only IPv6 addresses, the Mac's code now also carries the address devices there can use to reach it, which Fieldbook for iPhone build 19 tries. When the Mac has no address to type, it says to scan the code instead. The Mac no longer shows (or puts in its code) the 192.0.0.2 address every device on such a hotspot has. - **File Transfers:** while receiving, the Mac's address and code follow it to a new network. - **Send to Another Fieldbook:** Cancel, or a connection that drops, while the key is being checked no longer says "The key didn't match", and a Fieldbook that stops answering after connecting now says that. With Local Network turned off for Fieldbook, the list of nearby Fieldbooks says so instead of looking forever. - **File Transfers:** a send whose bytes have all gone, but that gets no answer, stops after 2 minutes instead of 12, and says everything was sent but not confirmed, so you check the other side before sending again.

Your day and your meeting time from Calendar, Help Me Answer that answers the question they just asked, and Check for Conflicts for each customer.
### Added - **New in Fieldbook 2.3.1:** shown once after updating, a short note over the main window with this update's two big things: **Today and Meeting Time**, with **Turn On Today…** and **Open Meeting Time**, and **Help Me Answer** answering their question, with **Check for Conflicts**. **Got It** closes it. - **Today:** your day from Calendar in a column beside any page; click **Today** in the toolbar to show or hide it. Each event shows its calendar's color, what you recorded and for how long, what's on now with **Record** and **Join**, briefs that are ready, and **Overlaps** where two clash. Personal and family calendars show too, so you can spot clashes, but never count as meetings. **‹ ›** steps through days. The window widens to make room, or on a full screen the sidebar folds away. It's off until you turn it on in **Settings › Modules**; Fieldbook asks for Calendars access then. - **Add Notes…:** for a meeting on your calendar that's over and wasn't recorded, **Add Notes…** in **Today** makes a notes-only meeting for it at once, named, dated, and filed from the invite, and opens it on your notes. The row then shows **Notes**, and **Meeting Time** counts it once, with the invite's time. - **Meeting Time:** a page in the sidebar, above **My To-dos**: how many meetings you had and for how long, this week, each week, and the fiscal year so far, in customer, internal, and other meetings. Tiles for the year, a bar for each week (meetings or hours) with your weekly average, and each week's meetings when you open it. **By customer** lists each customer's meetings, hours, this week, and weekly average, with its last 12 weeks. **Check these** lists recordings over 3 hours and meetings without a length. It counts the meetings you recorded, imported, or typed notes for and, with **Today** on, the meetings on the calendars you count as meetings that you didn't record, each meeting once (an event longer than 12 hours, such as a kickoff set as one event across days, isn't counted). Archived meetings count; nothing is sent to the AI. **This week** at the bottom of **Today** opens it. Turn it off in **Settings › Modules**. - **Meeting time on each Account page:** under the customer's name, one line with this week's meetings, the fiscal year's meetings and hours, the weekly average, and the last 12 weeks. **Meeting Time ›** opens that customer on the **Meeting Time** page. In General mode it's on each folder's **Folder Summary**. - **Your next meetings in the menu bar:** with **Today** on, the menu-bar menu lists your next three meetings under **Next Meeting** (tomorrow's with the day), and while **Meeting Time** is on, this week's meetings and hours. Click one to open **Today** on its day. - **By the numbers in Year in Review:** under the title, the picked fiscal year's meetings, hours, and weekly average, counted as **Meeting Time** counts them. Counted on your Mac and never sent to the AI. - **Calendars (Settings › Meetings):** choose which calendars show in **Today** and which count as meetings (at first only your work calendar), and a date to count meetings from. It works with **Detect meetings** off. - **Questions heard in a call:** while you record, the live draft spots the questions the other side asks, on this Mac with no AI. The newest shows on one line above **Help Me Answer**, with how many were heard; a **?** beside a **Them** line marks where one was asked. The **▾** menu on that line lists the last three, and choosing one answers it. - **Suggest a Question:** in the **▾** menu above **Help Me Answer**, a few questions you could ask next, for discovery calls. They show under **Questions to ask**. - **Check for Conflicts:** on a customer's **Account** page, after the executive summary, **Check for Conflicts** finds facts its meetings, notes, emails, files, and reports state differently, such as seats or a go-live date. Each is one line with its values and kind (**Disagree**, **Changed?**, or **Reports differ**); open it for each version with its date, source, and quote. **Which is right?** lets you use one value (and note it, dated, in your account notes, so later checks know; choosing differently or reopening it takes that line out again), mark both right or resolved, or dismiss it; settled ones wait greyed at the bottom. Checked only when you ask; **Update** sends only what's new. **Copy › Conflicts** copies the list. In General mode it's **Folder conflicts**; turn it off in **Settings › Modules**. - **Reports that differ:** when a customer's reports from about the same time give a different ARR, renewal, seats, or employees, it's listed under **Conflicts** without asking the AI, and the customer status figure shows a **⚠** (hover for the other value). - **Check for conflicts in Update All** (**Settings › AI**, off unless you turn it on): **Update All** also checks a customer's conflicts again when something's new.
### Changed - **Settings › Meetings › Calendar:** **Use calendar** is now **Use calendar to name and file recordings**, and its note says what reaches the AI: a meeting named from an event keeps its title and invitees' names, which go with that meeting when you use AI, and a brief you prepare also sends the invite's agenda. Your calendar stays on this Mac and is never changed. - **Fiscal year starts in** (**Settings › General**) also sets the years in **Meeting Time**. - What macOS shows when Fieldbook asks for Calendars, and **Settings › Permissions › Calendars**, now mention showing your day and counting your meetings, and what goes to the AI with a meeting named from an event. - **Help › Save Diagnostic Report…** also says whether **Today** and **Meeting Time** are on, the Calendars access, how many calendars show and count, and when the calendar was last read: counts only, never a calendar's name or an event. - **Help Me Answer and conflicts:** it's told which facts are still in dispute, so it gives both values or says you'll confirm instead of stating one as fact; for one you settled, it uses your answer. - **Help Me Answer answers their question:** the button and **Control-Option-H** now answer the newest question they asked, under **They asked**: a short answer to say first, in bold (yes or no first when your material supports it, otherwise that you'll confirm it), a few facts behind it, and **Check** lines for anything to confirm before you rely on it, instead of points to say next. It reads the last words they said before answering, and uses passages from the customer's earlier meetings and **Files** that match the question, found on this Mac; **From** links open the meeting at that point, the file, or the licensing source. With no question heard, it says so. Paused, the button waits until you resume the live draft.
### Fixed - **A meeting's title in a narrow window:** with the live draft open, the title no longer breaks inside a word; when it doesn't fit on one line with the folder, **Move To**, and **About**, those go on the line under it. - **Help Me Answer with Apple's on-device model or a small local model:** in a busy call it no longer stops as too long; it sends less of the call, the account summary, and the passages, to fit the model.
